name: Graft
text:
Decision: We should build a single, shared "Memory Map" document that links every key idea, person, or event we discuss to its core meaning in plain language—no jargon, no hidden files.

Why? Because recalling by meaning works best when the brain sees how things connect. A map makes those links visible at a glance, so we’re not digging through scattered notes later. It also forces us to clarify ideas upfront, which catches gaps early.

Trade-off: We accept that this map will start messy and need constant pruning. But the alternative—leaving ideas unlinked—guarantees they’ll stay unembedded in memory. The mess is temporary; the payoff is permanent access.
